segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Bloomberg's in-house economists just dropped a savage new report that traded their standard China cheerleading for some doom,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: contending that China, quote, may never overtake the U.S. economy.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Meanwhile, the U.S. Commerce Secretary is now warning China has become, quote,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: uninvestable for foreign companies who had long seen it as a free market paradise.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: So this is a big deal because for 35 years now, it has been an article of faith that China was going to inherit the earth.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: China's rise was inevitable, and we were all living on borrowed time.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Now, don't get me wrong, we are living on borrowed time.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: The disastrous policies made since the 2008 crisis, really since Richard Nixon,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: are putting us on an unsustainable path to permanent stagflation,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: flattening our growth prospects until we finally hit that financial singularity that is too big to bail out.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: The problem is China is headed to the same place, maybe even faster.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: I've done a couple of recent videos on China's rapid collapse.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: In short, Xi channeled trillions to politically favored industries at the expense of the dynamic bits of the economy,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: leading to both manufacturing and property now in free fall.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Those two sectors make up half of China's economy, much more than the U.S.,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: so that's dragging the entire country down,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: leading to rising joblessness, especially among the young who always get fired first.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: And, as in this country, financial and bank failures spreading like wildfire.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Bigger and bigger they march towards that moment, Beijing can't bail them all out.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Now, Bloomberg takes this clown show and runs with it, citing deep-seated structural problems,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: predicting a slower China for decades to come.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Specifically, they now think China could momentarily pip the U.S. sometime in the 2040s,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: but then immediately fall behind again as China's population shrivels,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: thanks to their idiotic one-child policy that appears to have become a social norm.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: So, seven years after one-child ended, China's currently sporting 1.09 births per woman.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: For a sense, if that continued for a generation, or for three generations, a century,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: China's population would drop eight-fold, to about half what it is in the U.S.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Now, keep in mind, that doesn't mean China's poor, it simply means they're number two,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: maybe number three if India keeps plugging away,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: which doesn't really matter day-to-day, it's more of a prestige and power thing,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: but it is a big change from the doomsday predictions of the past decades,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: and it suggests that China may already be past its peak of power.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: So, what's next?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: I think Bloomberg's being short-sighted, Xi is not immortal,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: and China has a lot more free-market bureaucrats than the U.S., or, God forbid, Europe.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Yes, China's in for some lean days, and those would hit a lot of poor countries like Africa,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: who depend on exports to China.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: But Xi himself has got a lot of opposition inside the Chinese government,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: despite building a personal police state, so he could retire surprisingly soon.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Moreover, the victory laps are delusional, because unless the West reverses our rapid plunge into socialism,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: the Asian policy mix will win, whether or not China's on board.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: So, what we see in Korea, Singapore, or Taiwan, where the economy is nurtured because it is the social safety net,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: because prosperity leads to the rest, rather than today's West,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: which crushes the real economy to buy votes or to fund activists who prefer to burn things instead.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: Okay, we'll be watching.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: See you next time.
